overview.description: Tjuv (Swedish for 'Thief') is a fishing card game for two or more players. It is sometimes known as Tattare. Unlike traditional Casino, capturing is based on suit and rank hierarchy rather than numerical value. A unique feature is the ability to 'steal' captured piles from opponents if you have a matching card of higher rank.

history.origins: Tjuv (Thief), formerly known as Tattare, is a Swedish fishing game first documented in the 1922 rulebook Kortspelsregler till tidsfördriv och nöje (Wahlström & Widstrand). The name Tattare was a disparaging term for Romani and Swedish travellers; as a game name it alluded to an unjustified reputation for stealing. Ulf Schenkmanis used the name Tjuv in his 1988 book Kortspel & patienser. The game has remained a simple family and children's pastime in Sweden.
timeline: 1922: Documented as Tattare in a Swedish rulebook; 1988 Schenkmanis text uses the name Tjuv.
history.evolution: Has remained a simple family/children's game.

setup.deck: 36-card deck: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit (no 2-5). Rank: A (high) to 6 (low).
setup.dealing: Three cards to each player. Each player places their lowest card face up on the table (or one of equal lowest). With two players the dealer adds one card from the deck to the table; with three or more the dealer reduces the table to three cards then deals one more to each. Three cards face up on table; remainder forms the talon.

rules.objective: Capture the most cards by playing cards of the same suit and higher rank than table cards or opponent pile tops; the player with the most captured cards at the end wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. Play a card. If it matches suit of a table card and is HIGHER rank, capture it. 2. Can also capture an opponent's pile if your card matches the top card's suit and is higher. 3. If no capture, place card on table. 4. Draw to maintain 3 cards. 5. Game ends when talon is empty.
keyRules: Must be HIGHER rank in SAME suit to capture.
Can steal opponent's pile (top card rule).

strategy.basic: Capture whenever possible. Steal piles to swing the score.
strategy.intermediate: Remember high cards played. Save a high card to protect your pile or steal a large pile.
strategy.advanced: Defend your pile by capturing with an Ace (highest) so it can't be stolen (unless rules allow Ace stealing Ace?). Generally Ace is safe.
tips: Aces are powerful for locking a pile.
Don't leave high cards on the table if you can help it.

play_card.description: Play one card from hand: either capture table cards and opponent piles (same suit, higher rank) or lay the card on the table. Must capture if the played card is same suit and higher than any table card.
play_card.constraints: Legal during play phase. To capture: played card must be same suit and higher rank than table card(s) or opponent pile top(s); can also take opponent piles when capturing from table.

draw.description: Draw from the talon to restore hand to three cards after playing.
draw.constraints: Legal in draw phase when talon has cards; draw until hand has three cards.

drawSources.notes: Restore hand to three cards after playing; draw from talon.

edgeCases.text: Cannot capture only an opponent pile; must capture at least one table card to also take opponent piles.
New captures form a separate pile even if same suit as existing pile; cannot capture own pile.
If a player clears the table when talon is empty, next player has no capture and must lay a card.
Last player to play a card receives all remaining table cards as captured.

customActions.description: Game ends; winner is the player with the most captured cards.

engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 36 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and nine ranks per suit (6 through Ace), created by removing cards 2 through 5 from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for easy suit identification.
engine.rankDescription: Nine ranks per suit starting from 6: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank has specific value and importance in determining game outcomes.
engine.dealPattern: Three cards to each; each player places lowest face up on table (or one of equal lowest). Two players: dealer adds one from deck to table. Three or more: dealer reduces table to three cards then deals one more to each. Three face up on table; remainder is talon.
